newsitem.title: GERMANY: Parry says favours more moderate U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: Parry says favours more moderate U.S. growth.

text.p: San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Parry said on Monday he believed the U.S economy must begin to grow at a more moderate rate after growing recently above its potential.

Parry told a discussion after a speech to a banking group in Munich that he believed long-term annual growth should be around two percent and that some forecasts have put long-term growth at between two and 2.5 percent.

"That means for some recent period, we have seen the U.S. economy operating slighlty above its potential. That suggests to me that it is quite important for the U.S. economy to grow at a more moderate pace and one that would be closer to its potential," Parry said.
Parry declined to give his personal views on interest rate policy outlook in the United States.
